bindings.selection_reason: softmax 对每行沿末维归约（max、sum-of-exp）为标量并广播回该行：模式 'Softmax, row normalization, and row scaling have this topology'，直接命名 softmax 并含已验证骨架；提供寄存器级 reduce+broadcast、tile 对齐规则（W*itemsize%32=0、TR%8=0）与 fp16 widen-compute-narrow 的 3x 向量开销洞察（与 mixed_precision 关键设计点对应）。

source_anchors: Applies when > Each row independently reduces its last dimension to one scalar and then uses that scalar across the same row
Dataflow > reduce each row to row_max / broadcast and subtract / apply exp / reduce each row to row_sum / broadcast and divide
requirements.class_evidence: SPEC formula y[b,i]=exp(x[b,i]-m[b])/s[b], m[b]=max_j(x[b,j]), s[b]=sum_j(exp(x[b,j]-m[b])) is exactly the row-reduce-then-broadcast topology over the last axis; rows are independent (B rows parallelizable).
requirements.invariant: Kernel processes row-tiles [TILE_ROWS, MAX_N] fp16; per row the VF runs reduce_max→broadcast-subtract→exp→reduce_sum→broadcast-divide; each row's m,s are VF-local register scalars; rows distributed across cores via strided pl.range.

source_anchors: Validation status > validated skeleton for the tile-operation form. A vector-function form is a separate implementation choice and must be validated against the target SDK's current API.

Sizing the row tile — two alignment rules > The data tile [TR, W] is RowMajor, so W*itemsize must be a multiple of 32; the reduction tile [TR,1] that a dim=0 reduce writes carries layout=pl.DN, so TR*4 must be a multiple of 32
requirements.class_evidence: Pattern's validated skeleton is the tile-op form (pl.row_max/pl.row_sum writing DN [TR,1] tiles); our design uses the VF form validated independently by the official sample pro_ops/vf_api/test_softmax_tile_group_vf.py. The DN-reduction-tile TR%8 rule applies only to tile-op dim=0 reduce; VF register-level reduce writes no DN tile, so TR is not constrained to a multiple of 8.
requirements.invariant: Use @pl.vector_function + vf.* (register-level reduce/broadcast) rather than tile-op pl.row_max/pl.row_sum; the W*itemsize%32=0 data-tile rule is still honored (UB addresses 32-byte aligned, see §3) but the DN-tile TR%8=0 rule does not bind the VF form. TILE_ROWS=3 is legal for VF.

bindings.selection_reason: P0 最大 N=4096 在 UB 248KB 与 fp32 加宽约束下大概率超出单 tile，reduction 轴须分块流式更新 running max/sum。该模式给出与本算子直接相关的具体设计约束：列尾 mask 须在 max 之前、行尾 mask 在 sub 之后、用有限负哨兵 NEG_LARGE（-1e30）而非 inf（inf 在 PyPTO-Pro 不编译）、m/l/累加保持 FP32、全无效行需短路。与 vec-row-reduce-broadcast（单 tile 情形）形成互补，设计作用独立。

source_anchors: Where the tail mask enters > 1. mask the reduction-axis (score-column) tail -- before any max
Where the tail mask enters > 5. mask the row-axis tail -- here, not earlier
requirements.class_evidence: Reduction axis N is dynamic; the last fp16 register of each row is partial when N%128!=0 (column/reduction-axis tail). Row axis B is dynamic; the last row-tile is partial when B%TILE_ROWS!=0 (row-axis tail).
requirements.invariant: Column (reduction-axis) tail: the tail fp16 register is masked with vf.update_mask BEFORE pass1 reduce_max (mask-before-max). Row tail: set_validshape([valid_rows, cols]) narrows the row-tile; the VF inner loop runs only valid_rows rows, so the row-tail is excluded before any subtract (rows beyond valid_rows never enter the VF). The two tails are handled at distinct points (column-tail pre-max in VF, row-tail pre-load via set_validshape), not merged.

source_anchors: Tail and precision requirements > Keep m, l, and the accumulation for o in FP32 unless the official implementation for the detected target proves another contract
requirements.class_evidence: reduce_sum is same-type (fp16 src accumulates in fp16, per reduce_sum.md table1); N up to 8192 with fp16 accumulation would exceed atol/rtol=1e-3, so the sum (l) must be fp32. Max of fp16 values is exact (the max IS one of the fp16 inputs), so m stored as fp16 is exact; exp_sub internally casts both operands to fp32 (cast_f16_to_f32), so the exp(x-m) computation is fp32-internal.
requirements.invariant: row_sum (l) accumulated in fp32: exp_sub(reg_fp16, row_max_fp16, dtype=DT_FP32) produces fp32, reduce_sum on fp32 results accumulates in fp32. row_max (m) kept as fp16 (exact max) and used as exp_sub src1 which internally casts to fp32 for the subtraction. The effective compute chain is fp16(in)→fp32(exp/sum/div)→fp16(out), matching the SPEC cast chain.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §1 pass2 (fp32 reduce_sum) + 超越函数数值安全边界; test_softmax.py: pass2 VF; precision verified at N=4096 P0 case.
requirements.verification_method: runtime: torch.testing.assert_close vs softmax_golden_cpu at atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3 on [32,4096] (large N stresses fp16-vs-fp32 accumulation).

source_anchors: Use a finite sentinel, not -inf > Write the invalid lanes to a large finite negative value: NEG_LARGE = -1.0e30
Use a finite sentinel, not -inf > In PyPTO-Pro a module-level float("inf") does not even compile: it renders as the undeclared C++ identifier inff and bisheng rejects the generated kernel.cpp
requirements.class_evidence: Pass1 row_max accumulator must be initialized to the reduce identity (minimum). float('inf') is not compilable in PyPTO-Pro; the official softmax sample uses NEG_INF = -1e30 for exactly this purpose.
requirements.invariant: Pass1 row_max initialized via vf.full(-1e30, preg, dtype=pl.DT_FP16) before the register reduce loop; no float('inf') or float('-inf') anywhere in the kernel.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §1 pass1 init; §1 数值边界; test_softmax.py: softmax_rows_vf pass1 row_max = vf.full(NEG_INF, ...).
requirements.verification_method: static: grep kernel for float('inf')/float('-inf') returns none; NEG_INF=-1e30 present; runtime: correctness on rows with all-negative values (golden covers large_neg case).

source_anchors: Complete recurrence > m_new = max(m_old, m_chunk); alpha = exp((m_old - m_new)*scale); l_new = l_old*alpha + row_sum(p)

Status > Conceptual guidance only. The KB has no retained runnable PyPTO-Pro reference that validates the complete streaming QK/softmax/PV pipeline. The retained single-tile softmax sample validates only the case where an entire row fits one tile.
requirements.class_evidence: The whole row fits in one UB tile: fp16 [TILE_ROWS=3, MAX_N=8192] = 48KB/slot, double-buffered in+out = 192KB ≤ 248KB UB (§3). MAX_N=8192 covers the full dynamic range N∈[1,8192], so no N-chunking is required. The pattern's retained single-tile softmax sample validates exactly this case; the streaming recurrence (alpha rescale across chunks) is not needed.
requirements.invariant: No cross-chunk running max/sum rescale: m and s are VF-local register scalars accumulated within a single @pl.vector_function call over the row's registers (3-pass: max, then exp+sum, then div). No persistent UB m/s tiles, no alpha rescale. If a future design must chunk N beyond MAX_N, this recurrence becomes applies and requires persistent m/s + rescale.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §0 归约轴容量结论 (single-tile, no streaming); §1 (one VF call, m/s VF-local).
requirements.verification_method: static: UB budget §3 proves whole row fits one tile; no streaming recurrence code present; runtime: correctness on N up to 8192 (golden dynamic-axis case).

source_anchors: Use a finite sentinel, not -inf > The sentinel has one hazard, and it is the all-invalid row. On a row where every lane is masked, m_new is itself the sentinel ... so an all-invalid row must be excluded or short-circuited explicitly
requirements.class_evidence: SPEC shape_constraints require N>=1 and B>=1, so every row within valid_rows has at least 1 valid column; rows beyond valid_rows are excluded by set_validshape and never enter the VF. No row can be all-invalid (every processed row has >=1 valid lane).
requirements.invariant: No all-invalid-row short-circuit guard is needed: the VF inner loop bound is valid_rows (rows with >=1 valid column per SPEC N>=1), and the column-tail mask always selects >=1 lane. The pattern's all-invalid hazard does not arise for SPEC-legal shapes.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §0 shape constraints (N>=1, B>=1); §7 (valid_rows loop bound).
requirements.verification_method: static: SPEC N>=1,B>=1 guarantees no all-invalid row; runtime: N=1 and B=1 cases pass (golden covers N=1).

bindings.selection_reason: softmax 3-pass（max/sum/div）需在同一 in_tile 上多趟读、in/out tile group 跨行轮转，模式直接以 softmax 实现为验证骨架（'rotating input, output, scratch, and reduction groups in the retained softmax implementation'）。给出 slot 计数律（B×K≤32 mutex 上限）、轮转组 advance 时机、partial tile 须 set_validshape、auto_mutex 不覆盖 V 管内 scratch 须 vf.mem_bar 等具体约束。

source_anchors: Safe workflow > 3. Use a multi-slot tile group only when iterations are intentionally rotated

requirements.class_evidence: The 3-pass reads the in_tile three times (max, exp+sum, div) within one VF call; the in_group and out_group rotate across row-tiles (each row-tile load→compute→store). m/s are VF-local register scalars (not persistent UB tiles), so no rotating reduction group is needed.
requirements.invariant: in_group and out_group each have depth=2 (double-buffer); .next() advances once per row-tile iteration to overlap MTE2 load of tile k+1 with V compute of tile k and MTE3 store of tile k-1. m/s are register-resident (not rotated); the 3-pass over registers happens within one VF call on the current in_slot.

source_anchors: How many slots > required slots >= (overlapped beats) * (simultaneously live roles)

requirements.class_evidence: All VF intermediates (exp results, div results) are register-resident within one @pl.vector_function call; no UB scratch store→load between VF ops. auto_mutex covers the MTE2(load)→V(VF)→MTE3(store) cross-pipe dependencies via the in/out group mutex_ids. source_anchors: Widening a narrow-dtype reduction > The register-level reduce primitives (vf.reduce_*) are same-type ... There is no narrow-in / wide-accumulate reduce to lean on. The widening is yours to write.
Widening a narrow-dtype reduction > The order that holds is widen → compute → reduce, with the whole chain in the wide type, narrowing again only at the store
requirements.class_evidence: reduce_sum is same-type (fp16→fp16 accumulation); N up to 8192 fp16 sum exceeds 1e-3 tolerance. Must widen BEFORE the sum: exp_sub(reg_fp16, max_fp16, dtype=FP32) performs cast_f16_to_f32 then exp, producing fp32; reduce_sum on the fp32 result accumulates in fp32.
requirements.invariant: Widen→compute→reduce for the sum: exp_sub(dtype=FP32) widens fp16→fp32 and computes exp in fp32 (cast happens inside exp_sub, before exp, satisfying widen-before-overflow); reduce_sum on fp32 results. Narrow only at store: astype fp32→fp16 before store_align. Max is exact in fp16 (max of fp16 inputs is representable), so no widen needed for reduce_max.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §1 pass2 (exp_sub dtype=FP32 → reduce_sum fp32) + pass3 (astype fp32→fp16 before store); §1 数值边界; test_softmax.py.
requirements.verification_method: runtime: atol=rtol=1e-3 on [32,4096] (N=4096 stresses fp16-vs-fp32 sum accumulation).

source_anchors: Widening a narrow-dtype reduction > The transcendentals are narrower still ... vf.exp covers FP16 and FP32 only, and vf.exp_sub's dtype table has exactly two rows — FP16|FP16→FP32 and FP32|FP32→FP32

Widening a narrow-dtype reduction > layout selects interleaved lanes, not a contiguous half. ZERO takes the even lanes and ONE the odd ones, and reassembling a full narrow register means interleaving the two results, not concatenating them.
requirements.class_evidence: Input is FP16 (not BF16), so vf.exp_sub FP16→FP32 path is native (exp_sub.md constraint table: FP16|FP16→FP32 supported on 950). Each exp_sub call processes 64 of 128 fp16 elements (layout ZERO=even lanes, ONE=odd lanes); covering one full fp16 register needs ZERO+ONE calls, interleaved (not concatenated).
requirements.invariant: Per fp16 register (128 elem): pass2 uses exp_sub(reg, row_max_b, mreg_fp16, dtype=FP32, layout=ZERO) → 64 fp32 (even lanes) AND exp_sub(..., layout=ONE) → 64 fp32 (odd lanes); reduce_sum each, vf.add to combine. Pass3: exp_sub ZERO/ONE → div → astype(dtype=FP16, layout=ZERO/ONE) → vf.add to reassemble 128 fp16 (disjoint even/odd slots) → store_align. The astype/exp_sub layout ZERO/ONE semantics (even/odd lanes) are followed exactly per the corrected reading in precision.md.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §1 pass2/pass3 ZERO/ONE handling; §1 数值边界; test_softmax.py.
requirements.verification_method: static: ZERO+ONE paired calls, vf.add reassembly; runtime: correctness (no every-other-element error).

bindings.selection_reason: mixed_precision 属性路由：fp16 与 fp32 计算需各自 create_mask，mask 粒度随 dtype 变化（fp16=128 元素×2bit，fp32=64×4bit），须遵守 mask 宽度约束。

source_anchors: Why it works > a MaskReg is a fixed 256-bit object, and width is not a property of the register. It is the stride at which the consuming instruction reads it — b8 reads bit i, b16 bit 2*i, b32 bit 4*i
requirements.class_evidence: The design mixes fp16 ops (load_align, exp_sub src, store_align) and fp32 ops (reduce_sum on fp32 exp results, div). Mask width differs: fp16 mask = 128 elements × 2bit, fp32 mask = 64 elements × 4bit. A single MaskReg cannot serve both widths.
requirements.invariant: Two separate mask families: mreg_fp16 = vf.create_mask(pattern=ALL, dtype=FP16) / vf.update_mask(valid_lanes, dtype=FP16) for fp16-register ops (load_align, exp_sub src0/src1, astype fp32→fp16, store_align); mreg_fp32 = vf.create_mask(pattern=ALL, dtype=FP32) / vf.update_mask(valid_fp32, dtype=FP32) for fp32-register ops (reduce_sum, div on fp32 exp results). No MaskReg shared across fp16/fp32 ops.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §1 (mreg_fp16, mreg_fp32 declared separately); §7 tail mask counts; test_softmax.py.
requirements.verification_method: static: two distinct mask_reg objects with matching dtype per use; runtime: correctness (mask-width mismatch would corrupt every-other-element).

source_anchors: The rule > Casting, slicing, transposing, padding, concatenating, and any other data shape or dtype processing MUST happen inside the @pl.jit kernel. The wrapper may only validate arguments, read ... metadata, derive Python integers, use torch.empty to allocate outputs declared by its current contract, and launch one kernel.
What to do instead > .to(torch.float32) on input | load the native dtype into UB, then convert on-chip — pl.cast at tile level or vf.astype at register level (there is no vf.cast)
requirements.class_evidence: Input/output are fp16; all fp16↔fp32 conversion done inside the VF via exp_sub(dtype=FP32) and vf.astype (no pl.cast needed since widening is register-level). Wrapper must not .to() the tensor.
requirements.invariant: softmax_wrapper(x): assert x.dtype==torch.float16 and x.ndim==2 and x.is_contiguous() (or read stride); y=torch.empty_like(x); block_dim=min(get_platform_info().vector_core_num, ceil(x.shape[0]/TILE_ROWS)); softmax_tile_group_kernel[None, block_dim](x, y); return y. No .to()/.contiguous()/.reshape()/.movedim()/.t()/torch.zeros/torch.npu.synchronize on host. All fp16↔fp32 conversion is vf.exp_sub(dtype=FP32)/vf.astype inside @pl.vector_function.
requirements.planned_location: DESIGN.md §0 Wrapper边界外操作=空; §1 (cast inside VF); §5 (single launch); test_softmax.py: softmax_wrapper.
requirements.verification_method: static: wrapper source audit (only assert/empty_like/kernel[...]); runtime: wrapper runs as the single device op.

source_anchors: There is no exception > torch.empty is the only torch.* function a generated wrapper may call
